A skill describes a repeatable procedure with an evidence standard and a refusal list, and usually spans several steps that each involve their own prompting. seoAudit.description: Crawl public same-origin pages and inspect response, indexability, metadata, structure, link, and JSON-LD facts.
seoAudit.metaDescription: Run a free, anonymous SEO audit across public same-origin pages. Inspect crawlability, index directives, metadata, links, and JSON-LD evidence.
seoAudit.pageSubtitle: Enter a public URL to inspect the same-origin pages this synchronous run can collect. The result contains crawl coverage, neutral audit records, measured values, evidence, and the inspected-page inventory.
seoAudit.heroTrust: No login · No GSC · No saved scan · Static public HTML only
seoAudit.scopeShort: No account and no sign-up. One run collects up to about 950 public same-origin static pages — the crawler paces itself to at least 250 ms between requests and stops at four minutes — and fewer if your robots.txt asks for a slower rate. Larger sites return partial coverage, labelled as such.

errors.invalid_url: Enter a valid public HTTP or HTTPS URL. Private and local network destinations are blocked.
errors.invalid_request: Check the website URL, and if you added target keywords, keep it to five of up to 80 characters each.
errors.payload_too_large: The submitted request is too large.
errors.scan_failed: The public site could not be audited from this environment.
errors.scan_timeout: The synchronous crawl reached its execution-time boundary before a report could be returned.
errors.scan_in_progress: A scan is already running from this network address. If you did not start one, someone sharing your connection may have — the limit is per address, not per browser. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
errors.robots_disallowed: This site's robots.txt asks crawlers not to fetch its pages, so nothing was crawled. That is the site owner's choice and says nothing about the site's SEO.
errors.robots_unreachable: This site's robots.txt could not be read, so nothing was crawled. A crawler that cannot read the rules has to assume it is not allowed. Try again once the site responds normally.
errors.rate_limited: This network has run several crawls recently. Each one fetches hundreds of pages from the target site, so there is an hourly ceiling. Try again shortly.
errors.target_busy: This site has been crawled several times in the last hour, by you or by someone else. The limit protects the site being audited from repeated automated traffic. Try again shortly.
errors.quota_unavailable: Something on our side is down: the service that enforces usage limits is not responding, and this tool will not crawl a site without a working limit in place. This is not about your usage — nothing you did caused it, and nothing has been counted against you. Please try again shortly.
errors.unknown: The audit could not be completed.

seoAudit.partialCoverage: The crawler stopped at {reason}. Every record below describes only the pages that were inspected.
seoAudit.boundedCoverage: The crawler completed the discoverable same-origin static pages reached in this run. JavaScript-rendered output and URLs outside the observed frontier are separate evidence boundaries.
seoAudit.recordsBody: Each record names one measured condition, its tested and observed counts, the supporting page-level values, and any evidence limitation. Records are not scores, priorities, or instructions.
seoAudit.noVerifiableObservation: The crawl did not retain enough evidence to verify this record.
seoAudit.noMatchingObservation: No matching observation was present in the inspected set.

limitations.resource_not_observed_does_not_prove_abs: A resource that was not observed may be absent, unreachable, blocked, or outside the successfully fetched resource set.
limitations.static_response_directives_only: Indexability here comes from the collected static HTTP/HTML directives. Search-engine index coverage is not measured.
limitations.normalised_text_match_within_inspected_p: Duplicate groups use case-insensitive, whitespace-normalised text and include only inspected pages.
limitations.bounded_static_html_crawl_inlinks_only: Inbound counts include links in collected static HTML only. This record is not a definitive orphan-page claim.
limitations.uncollected_link_targets_not_classified: Only collected link targets with an observed 4xx/5xx response are included. Uncollected targets are not called broken.
limitations.static_html_json_ld_only: JSON-LD observations come from collected static HTML. Client-rendered blocks are not measured.
limitations.no_sitemap_collected_membership_not_test: No sitemap was collected, so sitemap membership was not testable.
limitations.display_width_approximation_rendered_pix: Approximated by display width, counting CJK characters as two. The rendered pixel width Google actually truncates by is not measured.
limitations.bounded_static_html_crawl_outlinks_only: Outbound links observed in the bounded static-HTML crawl only.
limitations.depth_from_bounded_crawl_entry_point_onl: Depth measured from this crawl's entry point only, not from every real entry point.
limitations.no_target_query_was_confirmed_for_this_p: No target query was confirmed for this page, so there is no query to report a position for.
limitations.the_submitted_page_was_not_collected_so_: The submitted page was not collected in this crawl, so no per-page query rows were requested.
limitations.target_page_query_rows_hit_the_row_cap_s: The per-page query rows hit this run's cap, so a confirmed query may be missing from the average.
limitations.search_console_reported_no_impressions_f: Search Console recorded no impressions for these queries on this URL in the window, so there is no position to band. That is not position zero.
limitations.some_confirmed_queries_had_no_impression: Some confirmed queries had no impressions on this URL and are not part of this average.
limitations.one_impression_weighted_average_per_quer: One impression-weighted average per query over the reported window. Low-volume and anonymised queries are withheld by Search Console.
limitations.search_console_returned_a_position_this_: Search Console returned a position this run cannot place in a band for this URL.
limitations.single_uncached_request_per_url_not_a_fi: One uncached request per URL from a single location. This is what the server did for this run, not what visitors experience on their own connections and devices.
limitations.redirect_destination_status_not_observed: Only redirect destinations this run also fetched were checked. A destination outside the crawl was not classified either way.
limitations.query_rows_hit_the_row_cap_so_the_report: The query rows hit this run's cap, so the reported total is short and no share is published against it.
limitations.share_of_reported_queries_only_banded_by: A share of the queries Search Console reports, each banded by one impression-weighted average position. Low-volume and anonymised queries are withheld.
limitations.page_rows_hit_the_row_cap_so_a_page_with: The page rows hit this run's cap, so a page that does have impressions may be missing from the list.
limitations.search_console_window_may_predate_a_rece: The Search Console window may predate a recently published page, which would appear here as a page that has never been shown.
limitations.robots_rules_read_for_one_search_crawler: robots.txt rules were read for a single search-crawler token. A group written for a different crawler is not reflected here.
limitations.breadcrumb_markup_presence_only_not_comp: Only whether BreadcrumbList markup exists. Whether it matches the breadcrumb a reader sees is not checked here.
limitations.static_html_img_tags_only_css_and_script: Only tags in the static HTML. Images inserted by CSS or by script are not seen here.
limitations.format_read_from_the_url_extension_only_: Format is read from the URL extension, not from the response. An image served as WebP from an extensionless URL is not counted either way.
limitations.static_html_meta_tags_only: Read from the static HTML meta tags only. Tags added by script after load are not seen.
limitations.heading_levels_read_from_static_html_in_: Heading levels are read from the static HTML in document order, counting from the page's first heading.
limitations.no_target_query_was_confirmed_so_this_pa: No target query was confirmed for this run, so there is nothing to compare the page's text against.
limitations.the_submitted_page_was_not_captured_so_i: The submitted page was not captured in this crawl, so its text could not be read.
limitations.the_page_text_extract_was_missing_so_no_: The page text extract was missing, so no part of the page could be compared to the query.
limitations.this_page_has_no_title_so_there_was_no_t: This page has no title at all, which is reported by its own check. There was no text here to compare to the query.
limitations.this_page_has_no_h1_so_there_was_no_text: This page has no H1 at all, which is reported by its own check. There was no text here to compare to the query.
limitations.token_sequence_match_on_the_confirmed_qu: Matched as a token sequence on the confirmed query. No synonyms, no stemming, and multi-word queries must appear adjacent and in order.
limitations.soft_404_needs_both_a_not_found_phrase_a: A page is reported only when it states a not-found phrase AND falls below the published body floor. A soft 404 with a long body of suggestions is not detected here.
limitations.no_field_data_source_was_configured_for_: No field-data source was configured for this run, so CrUX was never asked. This is not a statement that CrUX has nothing for the page.
limitations.crux_reported_no_field_data_for_this_met: CrUX reported no field data for this metric on this URL, which usually means too few real visits to publish a p75.
limitations.crux_had_no_url_level_data_so_these_are_: CrUX had no URL-level data, so these are the whole origin's p75 values. A fast page can inherit a slow site's numbers here.
limitations.crux_p75_of_real_visits_over_a_28_day_wi: CrUX p75 over a 28-day window of real visits. It lags anything shipped today by weeks.
limitations.no_target_query_was_confirmed_so_no_resu: No target query was confirmed, so no results page was sampled and no paid call was made.
limitations.the_provider_reported_no_item_type_list_: The provider returned no item-type list for this results page. That is a gap in the response, not a page with no blocks on it.
limitations.some_organic_items_were_unusable_so_this: Some organic items in the sample were unusable, so this is a thinner sample than a full page one.
limitations.one_live_sample_of_one_results_page_whic: One live sample of one results page. The same query sampled again can come back with a different set of blocks.
limitations.the_field_data_provider_rejected_this_de: The field-data provider rejected this deployment's credentials, so no measurement was taken. This is a configuration problem on our side, not a statement about your page.
limitations.the_field_data_providers_quota_for_this_: The field-data provider's quota for this deployment was already spent, so no measurement was taken. Nothing here is a statement about your page.
limitations.the_field_data_provider_did_not_answer_t: The field-data provider did not answer within this run's budget, so no measurement was taken. Worth trying again.
limitations.no_results_page_provider_was_configured_: No results-page provider was configured for this run, so no results page was sampled. Nothing here is a statement about the query.
limitations.this_runs_market_is_not_one_the_results_: This run's market is not one the results-page provider covers, so no sample was taken and no paid call was made.
limitations.the_results_page_provider_did_not_answer: The results-page provider did not answer this run, so no sample was taken. Worth trying again.
limitations.robots_rules_hit_this_runs_cap_so_a_disa: This run's robots.txt rules hit its own cap, so a Disallow may have been dropped before it could be read. The allowance checks are reported as unverified rather than as permission.
limitations.sitemap_urls_hit_this_runs_cap_so_a_decl: The sitemap hit this run's URL cap, so a declared URL may be missing from what was checked. Members are read in order, so what falls off is a whole late-alphabet section.
limitations.hreflang_targets_outside_this_crawl_were: Alternates outside this crawl were not classified in either direction. A cross-domain cluster shows only the part that was reached.
limitations.utf8_bytes_of_the_delivered_html_no_rend: UTF-8 bytes of the delivered HTML. No rendering is performed, so this is what was transferred rather than what a browser ended up showing.
limitations.external_links_counted_by_destination_no: External links are counted by destination, so one partner linked several times from the same page counts once.
limitations.no_page_type_was_confirmed_so_there_is_n: No page type was confirmed for this run, so there is no reviewed range to compare the heading counts against.
limitations.a_reviewed_range_for_the_confirmed_page_: A reviewed working band for the confirmed page type, not a documented rule. The range is published beside the count.
limitations.no_confirmed_query_or_no_captured_text_t: No confirmed query, or no captured text to compute a density over.
limitations.density_over_the_captured_text_only_and_: Density is over the text this run captured, not the whole page, and it is never used to decide anything.
limitations.no_page_type_was_confirmed_so_there_is_n: No page type was confirmed, so there is nothing to match the declared schema against.
limitations.the_submitted_page_was_not_collected_so_: The submitted page was not collected in this crawl, so nothing it declares could be read.
limitations.this_page_declares_only_site_furniture_t: This page declares only site-furniture types such as BreadcrumbList or WebSite. Whether it has usable structured data at all is check 7.1's finding.
limitations.a_reviewed_mapping_of_page_type_to_schem: A reviewed mapping from page type to schema type, not a rule. A page can legitimately be more than one thing, which is why this is a Tip.
limitations.declared_in_the_head_markup_no_lab_run_a: Read from what the head declares. No lab run and no network timing, so this says what will block rather than how long it blocked once.
limitations.whitespace_words_between_headings_not_a_: Whitespace words between headings. A page written in a script without word gaps is not measured here at all.
limitations.only_types_in_the_reviewed_required_prop: Only types in the reviewed required-property table are judged. A type outside it is left alone, so a clean result is not a statement about every block on the page.
limitations.slot_order_not_a_character_offset_and_ne: Reported by slot rather than by character offset, and never used to decide anything.
limitations.no_clicks_were_reported_in_the_window_so: No clicks were reported in the window, so there is no split to publish.
limitations.brand_terms_derived_from_the_property_an: Brand terms are derived from the authorised property and matched as substrings, so a query containing the name counts as brand.
limitations.this_page_has_no_h3_so_there_is_no_secti: This page has no H3 at all, so there is no section to measure. Whether the outline should have a third level is check 3.5's finding.
limitations.first_image_in_document_order_with_a_dec: The first image in document order, judged only when the markup declares a size large enough for it to be the image a reader came for. A static crawl has no viewport, and a 32-pixel logo mark is the first image on a very large share of sites.
limitations.crawl_incomplete_inlinks_unreliable: This run did not fetch the whole site, or a page carried more internal links than the crawl keeps, so "nothing links here" cannot be told apart from "this crawl did not see the link". No page is named.
limitations.faq_match_against_collected_paragraphs_o: Questions are matched against the headings and paragraphs this crawl kept, which is bounded. A page whose FAQ runs past that point is not judged.
limitations.similarity_measured_on_collected_paragra: Similarity is measured on the paragraphs this crawl kept, after paragraphs shared by most pages are removed as site chrome. Pages with little text left are not scored.
limitations.page_weight_is_one_lab_load_on_an_emulat: Measured by one Lighthouse load on an emulated mobile device, not by a real visit. A page that serves different bytes to different devices will differ.
limitations.abandoned_share_counts_only_urls_this_cr: Counts only URLs this crawl actually fetched. A URL with impressions that the crawl never reached is left out of both the numerator and the denominator, because "the site dropped it" and "we did not reach it" look identical.
limitations.image_weights_are_the_bytes_this_run_tra: These are the bytes this run actually transferred, capped at the budget — a file that reached the cap is known to be over it, but its true total was not downloaded. A CDN may serve different bytes to a different browser.
limitations.no_image_weights_were_measured_for_this_: No image weights were measured on this run.
limitations.the_page_declared_no_images_to_weigh: The target page declares no images, so there was nothing to weigh.
limitations.no_declared_image_could_be_fetched_this_: Every image this page declares failed to fetch, so nothing about their size is claimed.
limitations.no_index_status_source_was_configured_fo: No index-status source was configured for this run, so nothing was asked of Google.
limitations.the_sitemap_declares_more_urls_than_this: This sitemap declares more URLs than one run can inspect. A rate over part of the list would be a sample again, and this one's error runs toward reporting a failing site as healthy — so no rate is published.
limitations.this_site_declares_no_sitemap_urls_to_me: This site declares no sitemap URLs, so there is no declared population to measure coverage against.
limitations.the_propertys_url_inspection_quota_was_a: The property's URL Inspection quota was already spent. It is a per-site ceiling shared with every other tool pointed at this property.
limitations.this_grant_does_not_cover_url_inspection: This grant does not cover URL Inspection for this property.
limitations.the_index_status_source_did_not_finish_t: The index-status read did not finish within this run's budget, so no rate is published.
limitations.index_status_is_googles_own_verdict_per_: Each verdict is Google's own, read one URL at a time. Only URLs the sitemap declares are counted, on either side of the rate.

robots_resource.title: robots.txt resource
robots_resource.description: Whether the crawler successfully fetched and parsed a robots.txt resource.

sitemap_resource.title: Sitemap resource
sitemap_resource.description: Whether the crawler successfully fetched a sitemap and how many sitemap URLs it retained.

non_2xx_final_status.title: Non-2xx final response
non_2xx_final_status.description: Collected page journeys whose final observed HTTP status was outside 200–299.

redirect_chain.title: Redirect chain
redirect_chain.description: Collected page journeys that followed one or more HTTP redirect hops.

http_url.title: Non-HTTPS final URL
http_url.description: Collected page journeys whose final observed URL used a protocol other than HTTPS.

noindex_directive.title: Noindex directive
noindex_directive.description: Inspected HTML pages whose collected meta or X-Robots-Tag directives contained noindex or none.

canonical_missing.title: Canonical link not present
canonical_missing.description: Inspected 2xx HTML pages with no canonical link in the collected static document.

canonical_differs.title: Canonical target differs
canonical_differs.description: Inspected pages whose canonical aggregation target differed from the page subject.

title_missing.title: Title not present
title_missing.description: Inspected 2xx HTML pages with no non-empty title in the collected static document.

title_duplicate.title: Repeated title text
title_duplicate.description: Inspected pages that shared the same normalised, non-empty title text.

meta_description_missing.title: Meta description not present
meta_description_missing.description: Inspected 2xx HTML pages with no non-empty meta description in the collected static document.

meta_description_duplicate.title: Repeated meta-description text
meta_description_duplicate.description: Inspected pages that shared the same normalised, non-empty meta-description text.

h1_missing.title: H1 not present
h1_missing.description: Inspected 2xx HTML pages with no H1 element in the collected static document.

multiple_h1.title: Multiple H1 elements
multiple_h1.description: Inspected 2xx HTML pages with more than one H1 element in the collected static document.

sitemap_page_without_observed_inlink.title: Sitemap page without an observed HTML inlink
sitemap_page_without_observed_inlink.description: Collected sitemap-member pages with zero inbound links in the bounded static-HTML graph.

internal_target_http_error.title: Collected internal target returned 4xx/5xx
internal_target_http_error.description: Internal link targets that were collected and returned an observed client or server error.

json_ld_parse_error.title: JSON-LD parse error
json_ld_parse_error.description: Inspected static HTML pages containing JSON-LD blocks that could not be parsed as JSON.

page_outbound_broken_link.title: Broken internal links on a page
page_outbound_broken_link.description: Pages that link out to an internal URL the crawl found returning 4xx or 5xx.

page_not_in_sitemap.title: Page absent from the sitemap
page_not_in_sitemap.description: Collected HTML pages that were not listed in any sitemap the crawl retrieved.

title_length_outside_range.title: Title outside the reviewed length range
title_length_outside_range.description: Pages whose title text falls outside the reviewed working range. Google truncates by rendered width, not character count.

meta_description_length_outside_range.title: Meta description outside the reviewed length range
meta_description_length_outside_range.description: Pages whose meta description falls outside the reviewed working range. Google truncates by rendered width, not character count.

page_without_outbound_internal_link.title: Page with no outbound internal link
page_without_outbound_internal_link.description: Collected HTML pages from which the crawl observed no internal link to another page.

click_depth_beyond_reviewed_limit.title: Page deeper than the reviewed click limit
click_depth_beyond_reviewed_limit.description: Pages that took more clicks from the crawl entry point than the reviewed limit.

json_ld_missing.title: No JSON-LD block
json_ld_missing.description: Collected HTML pages that carried no JSON-LD structured data at all.

redirect_destination_error.title: Redirect destination errors
redirect_destination_error.description: Collected URLs that redirected and whose destination answered 4xx or 5xx.

server_error_response.title: Server error responses
server_error_response.description: Collected pages whose final response was 5xx, counted apart from missing pages.

fetch_without_direct_page.title: Requests that did not land on a page
fetch_without_direct_page.description: Collected requests that ended outside 2xx, or reached it only through a redirect.

average_response_time.title: Average response time
average_response_time.description: Mean first response across timed pages, from one uncached request per URL from one location.

average_click_depth.title: Average click depth
average_click_depth.description: Mean clicks from the crawl entry point across collected HTML pages.

page_without_search_impressions.title: Pages with no search impressions
page_without_search_impressions.description: Pages this crawl collected that Search Console never showed in a result during the window.

impression_share_top_positions.title: Impression share in positions 1-6
impression_share_top_positions.description: Share of impressions from the queries Search Console reports whose average position rounds into the first six. Low-volume and anonymised queries are not included.

impression_share_low_click_positions.title: Impression share in positions 7-10
impression_share_low_click_positions.description: Share of impressions from the queries Search Console reports whose average position rounds into seven through ten. Low-volume and anonymised queries are not included.

target_query_ranking_band.title: Current ranking band for the confirmed queries
target_query_ranking_band.description: Where this page currently sits for the queries confirmed for it, averaged across them and weighted by impressions so a query it is barely shown for cannot move the number. Read from a Search Console request narrowed to this one URL, not from the site-wide query list, whose position for the same query is the property's average across every page that ranked for it.

page_disallowed_for_search_crawler.title: Pages robots.txt blocks from search
page_disallowed_for_search_crawler.description: Collected pages that a Disallow rule in the site's robots.txt matches for Google's crawler. Read for one crawler token; a file can allow this run through and stop a search crawler.

sitemap_url_disallowed_by_robots.title: Sitemap URLs robots.txt blocks
sitemap_url_disallowed_by_robots.description: URLs the sitemap declares for indexing that robots.txt forbids Google's crawler from fetching. Counted from the sitemap rather than from collected pages, because a URL this run was forbidden to fetch never became a page.

page_without_breadcrumb_list.title: Pages below the root without BreadcrumbList
page_without_breadcrumb_list.description: Collected pages deeper than the site root that declare no BreadcrumbList in their JSON-LD. Presence only: this run keeps no visible breadcrumb trail to compare the markup against.

image_without_alt_text.title: Pages with an image that has no alt attribute
image_without_alt_text.description: Collected pages carrying at least one with no alt attribute at all. An empty alt marks a decorative image and counts as covered. Read from static HTML, so images inserted by CSS or script are not seen.

image_in_legacy_format.title: Pages serving images in a legacy format
image_in_legacy_format.description: Collected pages where fewer than 80% of the images whose URL states a format are WebP or AVIF. An image whose extension cannot be read leaves the ratio rather than counting against it.

open_graph_incomplete.title: Pages missing an Open Graph property
open_graph_incomplete.description: Collected pages that do not declare all three of og:title, og:description and og:image with content. Read from static meta tags only.

heading_level_skipped.title: Pages whose heading outline skips a level
heading_level_skipped.description: Collected pages where the heading sequence jumps past a level in document order — an h2 followed directly by an h4, for example. Levels are counted from the page's first heading and include headings that contain only an icon.

image_alt_coverage.title: Image alt coverage across the site
image_alt_coverage.description: Share of the collected pages that carry images and have an alt attribute on every one of them. Pages with no images are outside this denominator, so a mostly-text site cannot dilute its way past the bar. An empty alt counts as covered.

title_without_target_query.title: Title does not contain the target query
title_without_target_query.description: The confirmed target query does not appear in this page's title as a token sequence. Token equality, so "chart" is not found inside "charter"; no synonym or stemming set is applied.

h1_without_target_query.title: H1 does not contain the target query
h1_without_target_query.description: The confirmed target query does not appear in this page's H1 as a token sequence. A heading that means the same thing in different words is reported here and is not necessarily wrong.

soft_404_page.title: Pages that answer 200 while saying they have nothing
soft_404_page.description: Collected pages that return 200, state a not-found phrase in their title or opening text, and carry less body text than the published floor. Both signals are required: thin content alone is a short page, and the phrase alone is an article about error pages.

core_web_vital_lcp.title: Largest Contentful Paint (CrUX p75)
core_web_vital_lcp.description: The 75th-percentile LCP CrUX reports for this URL over a 28-day window of real visits, on mobile. Field data, never a lab estimate.

core_web_vital_inp.title: Interaction to Next Paint (CrUX p75)
core_web_vital_inp.description: The 75th-percentile INP CrUX reports for this URL over a 28-day window of real visits, on mobile. Measures how long the page took to respond to a real tap or click.

core_web_vital_cls.title: Cumulative Layout Shift (CrUX p75)
core_web_vital_cls.description: The 75th-percentile CLS CrUX reports for this URL over a 28-day window of real visits, on mobile. Unitless; counts content moving after the reader began reading.

core_web_vital_ttfb.title: Time to First Byte (CrUX p75)
core_web_vital_ttfb.description: The 75th-percentile TTFB CrUX reports for this URL over a 28-day window of real visits, on mobile. Server and network time, not page time.

ai_answer_block_present.title: An AI answer block appeared on the results page
ai_answer_block_present.description: The provider's item-type list for one live sample of the results page included an AI answer block. Presence only — whether it fully answers the query is a content judgement this run does not make.

no_community_result_present.title: No community result appeared on the results page
no_community_result_present.description: One live sample of the results page carried no forum, Q&A or video result, which says the audience for this query is being served by publishers rather than by each other.

hreflang_target_http_error.title: Pages whose hreflang alternate does not resolve
hreflang_target_http_error.description: Collected pages declaring an hreflang alternate that answers 4xx or 5xx. Only alternates this run also fetched are classified; one outside the crawl is reported as unclassified, never as valid.

content_to_code_ratio.title: Share of the delivered HTML that is visible text
content_to_code_ratio.description: UTF-8 bytes of visible text over UTF-8 bytes of the delivered document, measured without rendering. Published as a weight hint; no threshold is applied.

external_link_follow_mix.title: Outbound links and how many are nofollow
external_link_follow_mix.description: External links counted by destination rather than by anchor, so one partner linked from the nav, the body and the footer counts once. Includes links opening in a new tab without rel=noopener.

h2_count_outside_reviewed_range.title: H2 count outside the reviewed range
h2_count_outside_reviewed_range.description: The number of H2 headings sits outside the range reviewed for the confirmed page type. The range is published with the finding: it is a working band, not a documented rule.

h3_count_outside_reviewed_range.title: H3 count outside the reviewed range
h3_count_outside_reviewed_range.description: The number of H3 headings sits outside the range reviewed for the confirmed page type. Read it against the H2 count rather than on its own.

target_query_density.title: Target query density over the captured text
target_query_density.description: How often the confirmed query appears in the text this run captured, as a share of that text. Published, never judged: density is not a documented ranking signal.

schema_type_unmatched_to_page_type.title: Declared schema type does not match the confirmed page type
schema_type_unmatched_to_page_type.description: The page declares structured data, but not a type from the reviewed set for the page type you confirmed. Site-furniture types such as BreadcrumbList and WebSite are ignored when deciding.

render_blocking_head_resource.title: Pages with render-blocking resources in the head
render_blocking_head_resource.description: Stylesheets without a non-screen media, and script tags with src carrying neither async nor defer, declared in the head. Both stop the parser where they sit. Read from the markup, not from a lab run.

first_image_lazy_loaded.title: Pages whose first image defers its own load
first_image_lazy_loaded.description: The first image in document order carries loading=lazy. A static crawl has no viewport, so document order stands in for the fold.

thin_section_under_h3.title: Pages whose H3 sections are thin
thin_section_under_h3.description: Average words of body text under each H3, segmented at heading boundaries. Counted in whitespace words, so a page written in a script without word gaps is not measured here.

json_ld_missing_required_property.title: Pages declaring a type without its required properties
json_ld_missing_required_property.description: A declared JSON-LD type is missing a property the reviewed table lists as required for it. Types outside that table are not judged rather than assumed complete.

target_query_first_appearance.title: Where the target query first appears
target_query_first_appearance.description: The first slot containing the confirmed query, in the order a reader meets them: title, H1, opening text, sub-headings, description. Published, never judged.

non_brand_click_share.title: Share of clicks not from the site's own name
non_brand_click_share.description: Clicks from queries that do not contain a brand term, over all reported clicks. Brand terms are derived from the authorised property and matched as substrings, so "acme pricing" counts as brand. Published, never judged.

page_without_any_discovery_path.title: Page with no discovery path
page_without_any_discovery_path.description: Collected pages with neither an observed inbound internal link nor a sitemap entry, excluding the entry URL.

faq_schema_question_not_on_page.title: FAQ markup promises a question the page does not show
faq_schema_question_not_on_page.description: Pages declaring a FAQPage whose Question names were not found in the collected headings or paragraphs.

page_near_duplicate_of_another_page.title: Page near-duplicates another page
page_near_duplicate_of_another_page.description: Pages whose distinctive text overlaps another collected page at or above the reviewed threshold, after site chrome is removed.

page_total_transfer_bytes.title: Total page transfer weight
page_total_transfer_bytes.description: The sum of every network request PageSpeed's Lighthouse run transferred while loading the target page.

abandoned_url_impression_share.title: Impression share on abandoned URLs
abandoned_url_impression_share.description: Share of reported impressions landing on URLs this crawl fetched and found gone or redirected.

image_over_transfer_budget.title: Image over the transfer budget
image_over_transfer_budget.description: Images on the target page whose transferred bytes reached or passed the reviewed per-image budget.

sitemap_url_not_indexed.title: Declared URL Google is not showing
sitemap_url_not_indexed.description: URLs the sitemap declares whose URL Inspection verdict is anything other than indexed.

evidence.title: Title text
evidence.expected_schema_types: Reviewed types for this page type

seoAudit.pagesBody: {count} page journeys were retained by this synchronous crawl. The inventory is collapsed by default; expand it to inspect direct projections from those responses.
seoAudit.howIntro: This is a formal free audit with no login required. The synchronous execution path retains necessary safeguards for time, downloads, redirects, concurrency, and private-network access.
seoAudit.step1Text: The submitted HTTP or HTTPS URL is normalised to its public origin; credentials, private networks, and unsafe destinations are rejected.
seoAudit.step2Text: The crawler reads robots.txt and sitemaps, collects as many same-origin static HTML links as it safely can, and enforces time, download, redirect, concurrency, and request safeguards.
seoAudit.step3Text: Collected page facts are grouped into neutral records and an inspectable page inventory. No score, priority, or remediation text is generated.
seoAudit.signalsBody: The free report is limited to facts available from this synchronous public crawl.
seoAudit.signal1Body: robots.txt and sitemap observations, HTTP statuses, redirect hops, protocols, content types, and explicit stop reasons.
seoAudit.signal2Body: Static meta/X-Robots directives and canonical targets from collected 2xx HTML responses.
seoAudit.signal3Body: Observed title and meta-description presence plus repeated normalised text across inspected pages.
seoAudit.signal4Body: H1 counts, word counts, crawl depth, inbound/outbound link counts, sitemap membership, and collected target responses.
seoAudit.signal5Body: Declared JSON-LD types and parse errors found in collected static HTML.
seoAudit.method1Body: Each record has a stable ID, category, neutral state, tested count, and observed count.
seoAudit.method2Body: Expandable observations retain the inspected URL and the exact projected values used by the record.
seoAudit.method3Body: Partial coverage, static-only collection, uncollected targets, and resource-fetch uncertainty stay visible in the report.
seoAudit.limitsTitle: Not measured by this public synchronous audit
seoAudit.limit1Body: The tool does not connect to GSC and does not claim that a page is indexed, ranking, or receiving traffic.
seoAudit.limit2Body: This tool does not execute page JavaScript and produces no Lighthouse or mobile-render results. The Agent audit reads CrUX field data for the submitted page when a key is configured; this public tool does not.
seoAudit.limit3Title: A complete inventory for very large sites
seoAudit.limit3Body: The synchronous tool collects as much as the current run can safely cover. Large sites may receive partial coverage; truly large site-wide crawls require a future asynchronous job version.
seoAudit.useCasesBody: The report preserves the same factual fields for every submitted site and makes coverage visible beside the observations.
seoAudit.useCase1Body: Record the public responses and page fields that the crawler can collect before a release.
seoAudit.useCase2Body: Inspect redirect journeys, final responses, canonicals, and collected URLs after a site move.
seoAudit.useCase3Body: Run the same synchronous audit again and compare the facts manually; this free tool does not store history.
seoAudit.comparison1Body: A collection of directly observed public-site facts with URL-level evidence and an explicit collection scope.
seoAudit.comparison2Body: It is not a site-quality grade, ranking forecast, repair plan, search-console report, or exhaustive crawl.
seoAudit.faq1q: Is this a real site-wide crawl?
seoAudit.faq1a: Yes. The server really crawls your site — this is not a demo with canned data. One run reaches roughly 950 pages: the crawler waits at least 250 ms between requests so it does not overload the site being audited, and stops after four minutes. A site larger than that comes back marked partial coverage, and findings that depend on having seen the whole site are reported as unchecked rather than as conclusions.
seoAudit.faq2q: Does it require a login or GSC access?
seoAudit.faq2a: No. It reads only public HTTP responses and does not request site ownership, OAuth, GSC, GA4, or another provider account.
seoAudit.faq3q: Does the report include a health score or grade?
seoAudit.faq3a: No. It contains neutral audit records, measured values, observed counts, URL evidence, and limitations only.
seoAudit.faq4q: Does it provide recommendations or a fix list?
seoAudit.faq4a: No. The public result records what was observed. It does not produce remediation advice, priorities, diagnoses, or an action plan.
seoAudit.faq5a: The crawler may stop because of time, downloads, redirects, concurrency, request safety, robots.txt, site responses, or synchronous runtime capacity. The stop reason remains visible.
seoAudit.faq6a: Only their collected static HTTP/HTML response is inspected. Content and links added only after client-side JavaScript runs are outside the evidence set.
seoAudit.faq7q: Does an uncollected link mean the target is broken?
seoAudit.faq7a: No. A target is recorded as an HTTP error only when the crawler actually collected it and observed a 4xx or 5xx final response.
seoAudit.faq8a: No. The anonymous response uses no persistence and is returned with no-store caching instructions.
seoAudit.relatedToolsBody: The separate internal link audit records observed links, crawl depth, and candidate orphan pages within its current synchronous collection.
seoAudit.articlesTitle: Keep every claim inside the evidence
seoAudit.articlesBody: Read how GenGrowth frames observed signals without overstating what the collected evidence can prove.
seoAudit.ctaTitle: Need stored runs and cross-run comparison?
seoAudit.ctaBody: The broader saved-project workflow is not currently open. This public audit remains anonymous and stateless.

trafficDrop.title: Traffic drop diagnosis
trafficDrop.description: Connect Search Console and see what actually changed in your own data, with the evidence behind every claim.
trafficDrop.metaDescription: Diagnose an organic traffic drop against your own Search Console data. Fixed comparison windows chosen by change-point detection, layered findings, and actions that name their evidence.
trafficDrop.pageSubtitle: Connect Search Console and see the change in your own data. We show the evidence and the explanations it is consistent with — we do not pretend to know the single answer.
trafficDrop.connectTitle: Connect Search Console to run this
trafficDrop.connectBody: This tool reads your property's daily clicks and impressions. Read-only, and never stored on our servers. The authorization stays encrypted in a cookie in your own browser, so a return visit does not start from the consent screen again.
trafficDrop.connectTrust: Read-only access. Disconnect any time — from this page, or from your Google account.

trafficDrop.inviteOnlyBody: Our Google consent screen is in testing right now, so only accounts on its tester list can authorize — anyone else would be stopped by Google rather than by us, which is why we say so here instead of letting you find out on their page.
trafficDrop.inviteOnlyCta: I'm on the tester list — authorize

trafficDrop.windowsFixedExplainer: Windows are chosen by change-point detection and cannot be adjusted by hand. Moving a window moves the conclusion — that is picking an answer, not diagnosing one.

sustained_decline.summary: A decline was located and it held: traffic stayed down across two non-overlapping weeks after the peak.

transient_visibility_anomaly.summary: Traffic dropped sharply after the peak week but came back — reported separately from a sustained decline, because it is not one.

insufficient_history.summary: There is not enough history to judge a decline. What the data does support is reported below; what it does not is left unclaimed.

no_material_decline.summary: No decline that meets the detection bar was found in this series.

trafficDrop.findingsIntro: Layered by evidence strength: an observation is a fact in your data, a hypothesis is an explanation the data is consistent with but cannot establish. We do not blur the two.

two_stage_decline.title: This is not one decline, it is two — with different mechanics
two_stage_decline.body: In the first stage impressions barely moved while clicks more than halved: click-through collapsed. In the second stage impressions finally fell, and click-through recovered. First people could still see you and stopped clicking; only later did they stop seeing you. Treating these as one event sends you to fix the wrong thing.

sustained_decline.title: Traffic fell after the peak week and stayed down
sustained_decline.body: Two non-overlapping weeks after the peak both came in far below it, which is what separates a decline from a bad week.

decline_concentration.title: The drop is concentrated in one group of queries
decline_concentration.body: A small set of queries accounts for most of the lost volume, rather than the loss being spread across everything you rank for.

high_impression_low_click_day.title: Your biggest impression day converted far below your peak week
high_impression_low_click_day.body: One day drew more impressions than any other in the period while producing very few clicks. That is what a click-through collapse can look like with no ranking change at all: a different set of queries arrived.

transient_visibility_anomaly.title: Visibility fell off a cliff for a few days, then came back
transient_visibility_anomaly.body: Impressions collapsed against what that weekday normally draws, then rebounded. Reported apart from the decline: a dip that recovered is not evidence of a sustained problem.

seasonality_unavailable.title: Seasonality cannot be assessed yet
seasonality_unavailable.body: A year-over-year read needs the same season last year, and this property does not have it yet. We do not estimate it. This check turns itself on once the history is long enough.

hypotheses.demand_cohort_receded: Demand for that topic may simply have receded. The data is consistent with it, but Search Console cannot establish cause. If those queries stay near zero next month while the rest recover, the explanation holds.
hypotheses.low_intent_query_influx: An influx of queries that rarely produce a click — often ones answered directly on the results page — would produce exactly this pattern. Search Console cannot confirm it; the query-level table is where you would check.

trafficDrop.actionsIntro: Every action names the evidence it rests on. Actions without evidence behind them are the thing this tool exists not to produce.

split_cohorts.title: Separate the affected query group from everything else before judging site health
split_cohorts.body: The headline number mixes two populations together. Split them and you will know whether your evergreen content is actually falling, or whether it is being masked by one group receding.

isolate_stage_one_ctr.title: Establish whether click-through fell because the query mix changed or because your results got worse
isolate_stage_one_ctr.body: The two have opposite fixes. If the mix changed — queries that never produce clicks arrived — there is nothing on your pages to repair. If your results got worse on the same queries, that is when page work is warranted. To tell them apart, take only the queries that already existed before the drop and check whether their click-through fell too.

pull_deploy_logs.title: Pull deploy records and CDN or server logs for the anomaly days
pull_deploy_logs.body: Search Console's index report trails its performance data, so the truth about those days is not in what we can read. If there was a release, a cache purge or a CDN incident, that is your explanation. If there was not, a temporary crawl fluctuation on Google's side is the more likely one, and you can let it go.

avoid_rank_recovery.title: Do not chase a rankings recovery because average position went up
avoid_rank_recovery.body: Average position is impression-weighted. When high-ranking queries disappear the number rises on its own, without any of your pages having moved. Optimising against it means solving a problem you do not have. For the same reason, do not prioritise this work by impression volume.

resolve_manual_action.title: Work the manual action first — it is the only thing here with a defined path back
resolve_manual_action.body: Open Search Console → Security & Manual Actions → Manual Actions and read which type it is. A manual action does not lapse on its own: the process is to fix what the notice describes and then submit a reconsideration request. Google's documentation for your specific type sets out what it expects. Everything else in this report is about where traffic went, and that question is not worth your time until this one is closed.

check_manual_actions.title: Go back and settle the Manual Actions page
check_manual_actions.body: You said you could not tell. It is worth another ten seconds: the Search Console API has no endpoint for it, so nothing in this report can see it, and it is one of the few things here with a defined path back — fix, request reconsideration, and it does not clear on its own. Make sure you are on Manual Actions rather than Security Issues in the same section, and on the property you selected — Search Console shows one at a time.

avoid_assuming_penalty.title: Do not treat this as a penalty and start deleting things
avoid_assuming_penalty.body: Google's own wording for algorithmic ranking changes is neutral: a drop does not mean your pages are bad. More often it means other results improved relative to them. Acting on a penalty you have not confirmed is how people delete content that was working, and there is no undo. Establish the manual-action status first; it costs ten seconds and it is the only part of this that has a definite answer.

avoid_disavow.title: Do not clean up backlinks or file a disavow because traffic fell
avoid_disavow.body: You have confirmed there is no manual action. Disavow is for one situation — a manual action that names your links — and this is not that situation. Google has said repeatedly that most sites never need the tool, and routine “toxic link cleanup” is a service people are sold rather than a fix. Filing one here spends money and can cost you links that were helping.

check_landing_page_indexability.title: Rule out a technical cause on the landing pages before reading anything into the split
check_landing_page_indexability.body: One group falling while the other holds is exactly what a robots rule, a stray noindex, a canonical pointing somewhere unintended, or a rendering regression on one template produces — they hit landing pages and leave the homepage alone. It is also the cheapest thing on this list to check and the cheapest to fix. Do it before you conclude anything about content.

resolve_security_issue.title: Work the security issue first — it outranks anything about rankings
resolve_security_issue.body: A Safe Browsing finding puts a warning on your results and an interstitial in the browser. That path suppresses clicks; it has nothing to do with rankings. Whether it is what caused your drop is not something we can establish, and it does not rule out something else changing at the same time — but it has a defined procedure, and nothing else in this report does. Find the flagged pages or injected code, clean it, confirm the hole is closed, and request a review from the Security Issues report. Until that is closed, rewriting titles and reworking internal links will not bring traffic back.

check_security_issues.title: Go back and settle the Security Issues page
check_security_issues.body: You said you could not tell. It is worth another ten seconds: the Search Console API has no endpoint for it, so nothing in this report can see it, and it is one of the few things here with a defined path back. Make sure you are on Security Issues rather than Manual Actions, and on the property you selected — Search Console shows one at a time.

unavailableReasons.query_read_not_performed: The query-level read did not run for this report, so this could not be computed. It was not checked and found clear — it was not checked.

unavailableReasons.property_totals_unavailable: Search Console did not return property totals for both windows, so we cannot tell how much of your traffic the query rows account for — and we will not assume it is all of it.
unavailableReasons.aggregation_basis_mixed: Search Console aggregated the two reads differently, which makes their totals incomparable. A ratio across them would measure the aggregation change, not your site.
unavailableReasons.coverage_below_floor: Too much of this property's traffic is withheld from the query report for a group-versus-group comparison to mean anything.
unavailableReasons.coverage_shift_too_large: The two windows differ too much in how much of your traffic is visible. That difference alone can manufacture the pattern this check looks for.
unavailableReasons.brand_sample_below_floor: There are too few brand queries and too few brand clicks for a percentage to be anything but noise.
unavailableReasons.cohort_below_floor: Too few queries cleared the impression floor to describe a migration.
unavailableReasons.read_truncated: One window returned more queries than we read. Rows arrive highest-click first, so what we missed is the long tail — the part this comparison is about. A number computed from the rest could point the other way, so there is no number.
unavailableReasons.group_without_baseline: One of the two groups had no clicks in the earlier window, so its change has no denominator. Most often the brand list matched everything, leaving nothing on the other side.
unavailableReasons.brand_group_not_observable_after: Brand queries were there before and are absent now. That is not the same as brand traffic ending: Search Console withholds low-volume queries, and the threshold is well above zero. Both look identical from here.
unavailableReasons.no_top_ten_queries: None of the queries in this set were in the top ten to begin with, so there is no migration out of it to describe.

limitations.history_below_twelve_weeks: Twelve weeks of history are needed before a decline can be judged. Below that we would be reading noise, so we do not report a verdict.
limitations.post_event_history_below_two_windows: The drop is real, but the property has not lived long enough past it to say whether it held. Calling it sustained would be a guess; calling it transient would be a different guess.
limitations.recovery_observed_within_one_window: Traffic came back within the following weeks, so this is reported as a short anomaly rather than a sustained decline.
limitations.query_breakdown_unavailable: The query-level breakdown was not available for this run.
limitations.index_report_predates_event: Search Console's index report ends before these days, so whether the pages were temporarily de-indexed can be neither confirmed nor ruled out here. Deploy and CDN logs are where that is settled.
limitations.site_below_detection_floor: This property has never had a week large enough for the detector to work on, so we cannot tell you whether traffic fell. That is different from telling you it did not.
limitations.returned_to_prior_normal: Traffic came down from a spike to the level this site held before the spike. A promotion or seasonal peak ending is not a decline, so none is reported.
limitations.recent_window_unfinalized: The most recent comparison window includes days Search Console has not finalised. Those days read low and may revise upward, so treat the newest figures as provisional.
limitations.event_within_unfinalized_window: These days fall inside the window Search Console has not finalised yet, so this may be the reporting lag rather than something that happened to your site. Check again in a few days before acting on it.

siteSignals.sectionTitle: What we can and cannot establish about a penalty
siteSignals.sectionIntro: Each of these comes with its own limits attached. None of them decides anything on its own, and adding them up does not either.

paths.unconfirmedTitle: One answer is missing, and it is the one that matters
paths.unconfirmedBody: Until that page is settled, this report will not tell you that you have been penalised and will not tell you that you have not. Both would be claims about something we cannot see. The traffic observations below stand on their own — read them, but do not read a verdict into them.
paths.issueReportedBody: Going by your report, work this first. A manual action is applied by a reviewer and a security issue by Safe Browsing; whichever you reported stays until you fix what the notice describes and submit it for review, and it does not expire or lift on its own. Read the entry for the specific type; Google's documentation for that type sets out what it expects. Whether it is what caused your traffic to fall is not something we can establish — we put it first because it has a defined procedure, and the traffic analysis below does not.
paths.noIssueTitle: These observations do not support a penalty
paths.noIssueBody: One thing is settled: you checked, and there is neither a manual action nor a security issue. Whether Google's ranking systems adjusted something about your site is a separate question, and it is one no tool can answer — there is no public signal for it, so anyone claiming to detect it is inferring. We are not going to. What follows is what we actually measured, and what each observation would also be consistent with. If it points at a technical cause, start there; those are cheap to check and cheap to fix.

coreUpdate.label: Where your decline sits on Google's announced timeline
coreUpdate.caveat: Context only, and it does not count toward anything. The detector works in whole weeks, so the event is a span rather than a date; announced updates roll out over weeks too. In a typical year those windows cover a large share of the calendar, so an overlap is as likely to be coincidence as anything else.
coreUpdate.eventWindow: Your decline happened somewhere in {startDate} – {endDate} ({dayCount} days).
coreUpdate.overlapOpenEnded: That span touches the start of {name} ({startDate}); Google did not announce when the rollout finished.
coreUpdate.noOverlap: That span does not overlap any update we have on file. This is not evidence that nothing algorithmic happened — Google adjusts ranking continuously, and only some of it is announced.
coreUpdate.tableStamp: Update list version {version}, last checked against Google's status dashboard on {verifiedThrough}.

brandSplit.coverage: Computed on the queries Search Console showed us: {beforeShare} of clicks in the earlier window, {afterShare} in the later one. The rest are withheld for privacy and are mostly long-tail.
brandSplit.shape_non_brand_declined_more: Non-brand queries fell further than brand queries.
brandSplit.shape_brand_declined_more: Brand queries fell further than non-brand queries.
brandSplit.shape_both_declined: Both groups fell by similar amounts.
brandSplit.compatibleWith: This shape is consistent with several things, and the numbers here cannot rank them:
brandSplit.explanation_technical: a technical fault confined to landing-page templates — a robots rule, a stray noindex, a canonical, a rendering regression
brandSplit.explanation_demand: demand for those queries changing, seasonally or otherwise
brandSplit.explanation_serp: the results page changing shape — AI overviews and other features taking clicks at unchanged rankings
brandSplit.explanation_competition: other sites moving onto the same queries
brandSplit.explanation_quality: Google's ranking systems reassessing the site's content
brandSplit.explanation_uniform: something affecting the whole property at once — availability, crawling, or indexing
brandSplit.truncated: One of the windows returned more queries than we read. The rows we did not read are the low-click ones.

cohort.label: Where a fixed set of queries sits now
cohort.intro: Fixed on the queries, not on the pages. A page's reported position is an average across every query it appears for, so it moves when the query mix moves even if nothing changed in the results — which makes “pages that fell out of the top 50” unmeasurable from that data. These are the same {cohortSize} queries in both windows.

recorded.lineage: Both are recorded as your observations, not as ours. Google publishes no interface for either page, so we have no way to verify them — which puts them on a different footing from the measured numbers below.

selfChecks.title: First, two things we cannot look up and you can
selfChecks.body: The Search Console API exposes four things: Search Analytics, Sitemaps, Sites and URL Inspection. Neither Manual Actions nor Security Issues is among them — Google publishes no interface for either page, so no tool can read them, including this one. Both answers are required before the report runs: they decide what it is entitled to say.
selfChecks.notice: Two cautions: Search Console shows one property at a time, so make sure you are looking at the one selected above; and these are two separate pages, so do not answer one from the other.
selfChecks.why: Why this comes first: these are the only two things in this report with a defined path back — fix it, request a review, and it does not clear on its own. Nothing else here has that. A report built without the answers has to qualify every sentence, and the heavily qualified version is the one you would read first and remember.

security_issue.where: Sidebar → Security & Manual Actions → Security Issues. This is where Safe Browsing reports malware, deceptive pages and harmful downloads.

quickWins.title: GSC Opportunity Finder
quickWins.description: Find the search queries Google already shows you for thousands of times that almost nobody clicks, measured against your own site's click-through curve rather than an industry table.
quickWins.metaDescription: Google already shows you for these queries thousands of times, and almost nobody clicks. Connect Search Console to find every one of them. Free, read-only.
quickWins.pageSubtitle: Google is already showing you for these searches thousands of times. Almost nobody clicks. This tool measures the gap against your own site — it does not claim to know what caused it.
quickWins.connectBody: We read your Search Console performance data — impressions, clicks, and average position, query by query. Read-only: we cannot change anything on your site or in your account. We do not store your results on our servers. The authorization itself is kept encrypted in a cookie in your own browser, so a return visit does not start from the consent screen again; it ends the moment you disconnect — here on this page, or from your Google account.

quickWins.tableIntro: Every query with enough impressions to measure, compared against what your own site earns at the same position. Sorted by the size of the gap. Each row is tagged with the checking path it is on — that is a triage, not a verdict.
quickWins.tableCaption: Search queries with enough impressions to measure, each compared against what your own site earns at the same position.
quickWins.downloadNote: The file carries the same rows, the same measured window, and the same blanks — a value we could not compute stays empty rather than becoming a zero.
quickWins.statusDone: Done. {count} queries in the evidence table.
quickWins.gapNote: The gap is expected clicks minus observed clicks, where expected comes from your own site’s rate at that position. It is a measured difference between two observed numbers, not a forecast of clicks you would recover by changing anything.
quickWins.tailNote: Tail probability assumes every impression is an independent trial at a fixed rate. Neither holds for search, and both errors push the same way — it reads as more unusual than the evidence supports. It is published for you to weigh, not as a test we act on.
quickWins.bandWarning: This band earns under 1% overall on your site. When a whole band is that low, the band is the finding — comparing queries inside it mostly re-describes it.
quickWins.curveIntro: What a normal click-through rate looks like on your site, at each position band, computed from your own non-brand queries. Published benchmarks say roughly 28% at position 1 and 2% at position 10; we tested those against a real site and found positions 4–10 earning a tenth of the published figure. Your own curve is the only one that describes your site.
quickWins.curveCaption: Click-through rate by position band, computed from your own non-brand queries.
quickWins.anonymizationBody: {impressionShare} of impressions and {clickShare} of clicks are not in the query report at all. Search Console holds back low-volume queries for privacy, so everything above is computed on a partial universe by construction.
quickWins.anonymizationUnknown: We could not read your property totals, so the withheld share is unknown. It is never zero.

exclusions.position_outside_bands: {count} queries averaged beyond position 21, where click-through is close enough to zero that a comparison says nothing.
exclusions.bucket_not_usable: {count} queries sit in a position band that did not have enough impressions or distinct queries to serve as a baseline.
exclusions.no_leave_one_out_baseline: {count} queries make up so much of their own band that removing them leaves nothing to compare against.

quickWins.limitationsTitle: What this will not tell you

limitations.serp_cause_unobserved: Why the CTR is low. A gap can mean your title is weak, or that searchers wanted something else, or that Google answered the query in the results page so nobody needed to click. We do not detect SERP features and those are a leading cause of exactly these gaps. Read a few of the actual queries before rewriting anything.
limitations.site_level_low_ctr_band: One or more position bands on your site earn under 1% overall. Every query in such a band sits below baseline for the same structural reason, so they are one fact rather than a dozen.
limitations.insufficient_bucket_sample: No position band had enough impressions and distinct queries to serve as a baseline. We would rather say we could not look than compute a number from four queries.
limitations.insufficient_query_sample: Your bands are measurable, but no single query cleared the 100-impression floor. That is a statement about sample size, not about your site.
limitations.high_query_anonymization_gap: A large share of your impressions and clicks never appear in Search Console’s query report. Everything here is computed on what Google returns, which is not everything.
limitations.partial_gsc_export: Search Console had more rows than we read. Rows come back ordered by clicks descending, so what got cut is the low-click end — which is exactly the part this table looks for.
limitations.brand_segment_insufficient_evidence: We excluded your brand queries from the baseline, but there are too few of them to say anything about the brand segment separately.
limitations.aggregation_basis_mismatch: The property total and the query rows were not measured on the same basis, so we cannot compute how much Search Console withheld. Search Console picks its own aggregation once a query groups or filters by page, and dividing one basis by another produces a number that describes neither.
limitations.anonymization_gap_uncomputable: We could not size what Search Console withheld: either the property reported no totals for this window, or the query rows added up to more than the property total. The two readings disagree, so we are not reporting a share rather than reporting a wrong one.

quickWins.emptyBody: That is not the same as “no opportunities”. See what we could not measure, below.
quickWins.storageNote: We do not store your results. Export or note anything you want to keep before you close the tab. We deliberately do not offer a before/after comparison: a re-run weeks later cannot separate the effect of an edit from seasonal demand, and presenting it as if it could would be the one claim this tool exists to avoid.

quickWins.actionsIntro: Every line here is gated on a number in this same report, and names the rows it came from. None of it predicts what a change would do — this tool does not model that, and the places where you would most want it to are exactly the places it says so.

apply_wording_candidates.title: Compare each candidate against the page it copies
apply_wording_candidates.body: For {candidateCount} of your queries we found a page on your own site, in the same position band, earning clearly more. The drafts further down rewrite the title and description in that page’s pattern. Open both before you apply anything: you are copying a pattern that demonstrably works on your site, which beats any template — but it is still a pattern, not an explanation of the gap.

open_serps_for_top_gaps.title: Search these yourself and look at what sits above you
open_serps_for_top_gaps.body: {serpRowCount} rows fall short of your own curve by more than a single click and have no comparable page on your site to learn from. The missing piece is the results page itself: an AI Overview, a featured snippet, a video carousel or a People-Also-Ask block takes the click before your listing is read, and we observe none of them. Search each query in a private window and note what sits above position 1. If the page is plain and your listing is still skipped, then the title and description are the candidate. The largest shortfall here is {largestGapClicks} clicks.

size_the_withheld_share.title: Find out how much never reached this table
size_the_withheld_share.body: Search Console withholds queries below an undisclosed volume threshold — here that is {withheldImpressionShare} of impressions and {withheldClickShare} of clicks, where a dash means we could not size it, which is never the same as zero. Open the Performance report and compare its own totals against the query tab. The difference is the part no query-level tool can see, and on a small site most of the demand lives there.

check_pages_report.title: Switch to the Pages report — most of your queries are too small to appear here
check_pages_report.body: {belowFloorCount} queries had fewer than 100 impressions in this window, against {measuredRowCount} that cleared the floor. One click either way would change their rate completely, so we leave them out rather than publish a rate we do not believe. Search Console’s Pages tab aggregates them: a pattern that is invisible query by query is often plain page by page.

read_low_band_as_one_finding.title: Don’t rewrite a low band one query at a time
read_low_band_as_one_finding.body: Positions {bands} earn under 1% overall on your site, and {lowBandRowCount} of the rows above sit there. Every one of them is below baseline for the same structural reason, so they are one fact rather than {lowBandRowCount}. Published tables predict 3–7% at these positions; we tested that against a real site and measured a tenth of it. Whatever is happening applies to the band — start there, not with the individual titles.

avoid_curve_as_law.title: Your curve does not fall the way rank tables say it should
avoid_curve_as_law.body: Positions {firstBand} earn {higherBandCtr} on your site, while {secondBand} — ranking lower — earn {lowerBandCtr}. That is not a measurement error, it is what your queries do: what people search for changes with the position you hold, and a lower band full of specific, high-intent queries can out-earn a higher band full of vague ones. It also means the baseline inside the higher band is weak evidence about any single row in it.

avoid_gap_as_forecast.title: The gap column adds up to {totalGapClicks} clicks. Rewriting will not hand them to you.
avoid_gap_as_forecast.body: The gap is expected clicks minus observed clicks, where expected comes from your own site’s rate at that position. Both sides are measured and so is the difference. It is not a forecast: nothing here models the effect of a change, and the leading cause of gaps like these is a results page that answered the query so nobody needed to click. Read {totalGapClicks} as the size of the question, not the size of the prize.

compare_with_own_page.label: Has a control
compare_with_own_page.hint: A page on your own site, in the same position band, earns clearly more. That page is the comparison — there is a draft below modelled on it.

read_the_serp.label: Check the SERP
read_the_serp.hint: Short by more than a click, with no comparable page on your site. The missing information is on the results page, which you can see and we cannot.

band_is_the_story.label: Band-wide
band_is_the_story.hint: The whole position band earns under 1%. These rows are below baseline for one shared reason, so rewriting them one at a time treats one fact as many.

gap_within_noise.label: Under one click
gap_within_noise.hint: The shortfall is smaller than a single click. Clicks are counted in whole numbers, so prediction and observation agree as closely as the unit allows.

at_or_above_curve.label: At or above
at_or_above_curve.hint: At or better than what your site earns at this position. Kept in the table as context, not as work.

faq.title: What this does and does not tell you

items.q: Where does the score come from?
items.a: Each check on this page is worth a set number of points; the score is their sum, restated out of 100. The weights are ours, not Google's — the number measures how well this page does the part it controls, not whether it will rank. A few conditions hold the score down on their own: a page that declares noindex, returns an error status, carries almost no copy, or is not about the keyword you gave. In those cases no amount of other work reaches a search result.

items.q: Why does the first check take minutes?
items.a: Your page is read out of a site-wide collection rather than fetched on its own. A second check on the same site within the hour reuses that collection and returns in seconds; after that the collection has expired and the crawl runs again.

items.q: Will a high count rank the page?
items.a: No. Where a keyword sits on a page is one input among site authority, page experience, competition and behaviour. This measures the input it can actually see.

items.q: How many queries can I check at once, and how do I type them?
items.a: Up to five, all in the one field, separated by commas — both the ASCII comma and the full-width one, and a newline counts too. Repeats are folded into one, anything past five is not submitted, and the field says how many it dropped. One query is marked primary: most fields covered wins, then the longer query, then the order you typed them. Topic focus in the score reads that one query only, so adding exploratory words alongside your real target cannot lower the page's score.

They are labelled, and that is all — no points either way. The test is mechanical: the hostname is split into labels and compared against what you typed. The result is published as an observation, never as score, because a brand term sits at a density that would read as thin for a topic term and judging the same number twice is not honest. A single CJK word has no Latin label to compare against, so it is marked not applicable rather than not matched.

items.q: Why is keyword density not scored?
items.a: Because two different denominators appear on this page and mixing them produces opposite conclusions. The per-query density is measured inside the captured text — title, description, the heading set and the opening passage — where a normally optimised page already sits near 20%, so the familiar 0.5%–3% band would call a well-built page keyword stuffing. The whole-page term tables use the page body's counting units instead. Both numbers name their own denominator, but they cannot be compared, so we report them and grade neither.

items.q: How do I read the whole-page term tables?
items.a: The page body is cut into one- to five-word combinations, with the top 15 kept for each length. Term density is occurrences divided by total units. Occupancy density is occurrences times phrase length divided by total units, so phrases of different lengths can be compared — overlapping occurrences are counted each time, which is why a long phrase on a page that repeats one word can exceed 100%. Function words are removed from the single-word table only; phrase tables keep them, because "the astrology of" is how people actually write.

The crawl reads the HTML the server returned, so body copy, components and links mounted by front-end script are invisible to this tool. It does not pretend otherwise: one check reports whether the body text is in the static HTML at all. When it is not, the word count and the coverage on this page were both measured under that condition — do not read them as what a browser finishes rendering.

items.q: Where does the search-results section get its data?
items.a: From a third-party search-results source, for the market and language you picked above, as one desktop sample of page one: who holds the top positions, whether you are among them, and how many carry sitelinks. Results move daily, so this is a snapshot rather than a ranking history or a difficulty score. It is also the one paid call this tool makes, which is why market and language are lists — an unsupported pair never leaves a request at all.

items.q: Does it work on Chinese pages?
items.a: Yes. Body length counts one unit per CJK character. Title and description length is measured in display width, with CJK characters counted as two, which lands closer to where a search result actually truncates. The term tables split on the same basis.

items.q: Where are my past checks stored?
items.a: In this browser only. It is not an account archive: clearing storage, switching browsers or signing out loses it. When one page has been checked more than once, the list shows how its score and coverage moved.

items.q: How is this different from the SEO Agent?
items.a: They run the same site-wide crawl. This tool reads the one page you named out of that crawl and answers around the queries you gave; the Agent reads the whole site. That is why the first check waits for the crawl, and why the same site checked again within the hour comes back in seconds. The report hands this page and its queries straight to the Agent.

fixes.title: What to change on this page
fixes.homepage: A homepage is judged on whether the primary term is unmistakable: put it in the title, the H1 and the first sentence of the body, and let the sub-headings carry the secondary terms rather than repeating the primary one.
fixes.product: A product page competes on specificity. Keep the product's own name in the title and H1, and let the target term appear where it describes what the product does, not as a phrase bolted onto the front of the name.
fixes.tool: A tool page is found by what it does. The title and H1 should read as the job the visitor came to do, and the opening text should say the tool runs here rather than describing it from the outside.
fixes.guide: A guide is found by the question it answers. Put the question's own words in the title and H1, and use the sub-headings for the sub-questions so a reader scanning them can see the answer is here.
fixes.basis: Guidance for the page role you declared. It does not change any count above, and none of it is a claim about ranking.

title.outsideRange: Width {width}, outside {min}–{max}, so it may be truncated or read as thin.

description.outsideRange: Width {width}, outside {min}–{max}, so the tail may be cut.

robots.noindex: Declares noindex ({directives}). This page will not be indexed, and no other check changes that.

charset.missing: No charset declared, so non-ASCII text can be read under the wrong encoding.
charset.fromHeader: The HTTP response header declares {charset}, which is the value the browser actually decodes with.
charset.conflict: The response header says {header} and the meta tag says {meta}. The browser decodes by the header, so one of the two declarations is wrong.

h1.tooLongClipped: The H1 is at least {width} wide (shown here cut to 200 characters), far past the common {max}.

bodyWords.goodUnits: The body runs about {words} characters, a full-length piece.
